public.label: 01 / PUBLIC · FIRM TECHNOLOGY
public.title: What keeps firms from adopting better technology?
public.desc: A manufacturing economy cannot close its productivity gap without measuring the technologies firms actually use and understanding the barriers to adoption.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Uneven firm-level capability and equipment use
Limited evidence on adoption barriers by sector
Interventions poorly targeted to firm readiness
results: Segment firms by capability and barriers
Target adoption, skills and financing mechanisms

private.label: 01 / PRIVATE · OPERATIONS
private.title: Where does an upgrade actually improve performance?
private.desc: Equipment expenditure alone is not productivity. Firms need evidence about bottlenecks, worker capability, financing and returns before selecting new technology.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: Technology spending without a business case.
problems: Bottlenecks hidden across the production line
Capital budget separated from skills needs
Benefits assumed instead of measured
results: Compare alternative process and equipment upgrades
Combine skills, financing and maintenance plans

public.label: 02 / PUBLIC · GREEN INDUSTRY
public.title: Turning the green transition into a firm-level programme.
public.desc: Climate goals become actionable when policymakers understand factory constraints, access to green finance and the incentives shaping energy and technology choices.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Energy and investment gaps vary across factories
Green finance and regulatory requirements difficult to navigate
Policy instruments disconnected from firm economics

private.label: 02 / PRIVATE · GREEN COMPETITIVENESS
private.title: When does a greener production line make business sense?
private.desc: For an exporter, clean energy and process efficiency decisions depend on lifecycle costs, buyer requirements, operational risk and available financing.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: Clean technology perceived as only a cost.
problems: Energy savings and upfront cost poorly compared
Buyer sustainability demands difficult to price
Green financing options not evaluated
results: Prioritise projects by payback and resilience
Align operational measures with buyer needs

public.label: 03 / PUBLIC · WORKER SERVICE MARKETS
public.title: Designing worker services that support better jobs.
public.desc: Employment, health and productivity intersect. A functioning worker-services market needs credible evidence on access, business incentives and service quality.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
public.problemTitle: Workforce needs and service incentives misaligned.
problems: Workers face barriers to reliable services
Factory value proposition not made visible
Programme effects insufficiently tested
public.resultTitle: A service model with measurable value.
results: Map worker needs and service delivery gaps
Align factory, worker and provider incentives

private.label: 03 / PRIVATE · WORKFORCE PERFORMANCE
private.title: Can worker wellbeing become part of operating strategy?
private.desc: Worker services should be assessed alongside retention, absence, service use, costs and longer-run productivity—not treated as a standalone corporate benefit.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: People costs measured, people value missed.
problems: Absence and turnover treated as isolated metrics
Worker service investments lack a testable hypothesis
No integrated performance dashboard
results: Link service quality with operating indicators
Compare costs and potential business value

public.label: 04 / PUBLIC · BUSINESS ENVIRONMENT
public.title: Removing the hidden costs of doing business.
public.desc: Better business rules are not only about reducing forms. Institutional processes, licensing, transparency and implementation capacity determine how well markets function.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Overlapping procedures and uncertain processing time
Weak feedback loops between businesses and agencies
Simplifications not tracked for actual use
public.resultTitle: A reform that firms can experience.
results: Monitor service standards and business confidence

private.label: 04 / PRIVATE · MARKET ENTRY
private.title: Making expansion decisions with fewer blind spots.
private.desc: An attractive market may still impose costly delays through registration, certification, permits, logistics and uncertainty. Strategy must price those frictions explicitly.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: Expansion plan ignores the cost of friction.
problems: Time-to-market assumptions too optimistic
Approvals and certification risks uncosted
Market-entry milestones unsequenced
results: Identify requirements and real transaction costs

public.label: 05 / PUBLIC · INCLUSIVE ENTERPRISE
public.title: Connecting rural producers with viable markets.
public.desc: Small producers often have capability, quality and market-access constraints at the same time. Enterprise development must link training to buyer demand and commercialization.
public.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
problems: Fragmented buyer relationships and information
Limited commercialization and quality systems
Training results not linked to viable demand

private.label: 05 / PRIVATE · SME GROWTH
private.title: Finding the next viable market for a growing enterprise.
private.desc: A smaller enterprise must choose products, segments and channels where customers will pay, supply remains reliable and contribution margins support growth.
private.ref: Synthetic teaching scenario. No client result is asserted.
private.problemTitle: Growth is driven by volume, not economics.
problems: Market segments and willingness-to-pay unclear
Channel and logistics costs mismeasured
Scale-up outpaces product quality and cash flow
results: Test product pricing and unit economics
